# Data Cleaning for the NCBI dataset

This dataset contains 44 samples from hourly measurements from 5 hours to 48 hours of C. elegans developments


```{r}
source("010_download_genomics.R")
```
```{r}
file_path <- file.path(
  "data",
  "GSE130811",
  "GSE130811_expr_mRNA_CE10_coding.tab.gz"
)

# Read compressed gene-expression data
expr_raw <- read.delim(
  gzfile(file_path),
  header = TRUE,
  check.names = FALSE
)

# Dataset dimensions
dim(expr_raw)
```
The dataset dimensions are $20392 \times 52$

Lets look explore the dataset
```{r}
head(expr_raw[, seq_len(min(6, ncol(expr_raw)))]) #looking at first 6 rows and colums

colnames(expr_raw)

str(expr_raw, list.len = 12)


```
```{r}
sum(is.na(expr_raw))# Total missing values


missing_per_column <- colSums(is.na(expr_raw)) # Missing values by column


missing_per_column[missing_per_column > 0] # Show columns with missing values

```
No missing data (hooray!)

```{r}
numeric_cols <- vapply(
  expr_raw,
  is.numeric,
  logical(1)
)# Identify numeric columns

sum(numeric_cols)# Number of numeric columns


if (any(numeric_cols)) {
  summary(expr_raw[, numeric_cols, drop = FALSE])
}# Summary statistics

```
```{r}
# Identify the type of each column
column_info <- data.frame(
  column = names(expr_raw),
  type = vapply(expr_raw, typeof, character(1)),
  example = vapply(
    expr_raw,
    function(x) as.character(x[1]),
    character(1)
  )
)

print(column_info, row.names = FALSE)
```

## Identify Genes and Time Points

The dataset contains raw RNA-seq counts. Before normalization,
we need to separate the expression measurements from the gene-width
information and identify the measurement times.

```{r}
# Extract gene identifiers
gene_ids <- rownames(expr_raw)

# Remove width column; retain expression counts
counts <- as.matrix(
  expr_raw[, -1, drop = FALSE]
)

rownames(counts) <- gene_ids

# Extract the hour from each column name
hours <- as.integer(
  sub("hr.*$", "", colnames(counts))
)

# Summarize samples and sequencing depths
sample_info <- data.frame(
  sample = colnames(counts),
  hour = hours,
  total_counts = colSums(counts)
)

# Inspect gene IDs and count matrix
head(gene_ids)
dim(counts)

# Number of measurements at each hour
table(sample_info$hour)

# Identify hours with repeated measurements
sample_info[
  duplicated(sample_info$hour) |
  duplicated(sample_info$hour, fromLast = TRUE),
]
```

## Selecting the Hourly Measurements

The dataset contains 51 RNA-seq measurement columns,
but only 44 distinct hourly time points. Seven hours
have additional measurements.

For the initial VAR(1) analysis, we retain one
measurement per hour, from hour 5 through hour 48,
and preserve the additional measurements for
possible future analysis.

```{r}
hourly_cols <- paste0(5:48, "hr")

# Retain 44 hourly measurements
counts_hourly <- counts[
  ,
  hourly_cols,
  drop = FALSE
]

# Store excluded measurements for documentation
extra_cols <- setdiff(colnames(counts), hourly_cols)
extra_counts <- counts[, extra_cols, drop = FALSE]

# Inspect dimensions
dim(counts_hourly)
extra_cols
```

## Normalizing Gene Expression Data

The dataset contains raw RNA-seq counts, which may differ
across samples because of sequencing depth.

To make expression measurements more comparable,
we normalize the counts using Counts Per Million (CPM)
and apply a log transformation.

```{r}
# Calculate total counts for each time point
library_sizes <- colSums(counts_hourly)

# Examine differences in sequencing depth
summary(library_sizes)

# Check that every sample has positive total counts

# Normalize counts using CPM
cpm <- sweep(
  counts_hourly,
  2,
  library_sizes,
  FUN = "/"
) * 1e6

# Log2 transformation to reduce skewness
log_cpm <- log2(cpm + 1)

# Verify dimensions and finite values
dim(log_cpm)

# Examine normalized expression values
summary(as.vector(log_cpm))
```


## Filtering Low-Expression Genes

Some genes may have little to no expression throughout
the developmental period. These genes may contribute
little useful information to our VAR(1) model.

For our preliminary analysis, we retain genes with
at least 1 CPM in at least 5 time points.

```{r}
# Reserve hours 41–48 for future testing
train_cols <- paste0(5:40, "hr")

# Filter low-expression genes using training data only
keep_genes <- rowSums(
  cpm[, train_cols, drop = FALSE] >= 1
) >= 5

sum(keep_genes)
sum(!keep_genes)

# Keep all 44 hours for the retained genes
log_cpm_filtered <- log_cpm[
  keep_genes,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

dim(log_cpm_filtered)
```

We can also calculate the percentage of genes retained.

```{r}
retained_pct <- mean(keep_genes) * 100

cat("Percentage of genes retained:",
    round(retained_pct, 2), "%")
```


## Selecting Highly Variable Genes

After filtering low-expression genes, we examine the
variability of gene expression across the 44 time points.

For our initial analysis, we select the 100 genes
with the highest sample variance.

```{r}
# Set number of genes
p <- 100

# Calculate variance using training hours only
gene_var <- apply(
  log_cpm_filtered[, train_cols, drop = FALSE],
  1,
  var
)

# Select 100 genes with highest variance
top_genes <- names(
  sort(gene_var, decreasing = TRUE)
)[1:p]

# Display first 10 selected genes
head(data.frame(
  gene = top_genes,
  variance = gene_var[top_genes]
), 10)

# Retain selected genes across all 44 hours
selected_expr <- log_cpm_filtered[
  top_genes,
  ,
  drop = FALSE
]

dim(selected_expr)
```

## Visualizing Gene Expression Over Time

We selected the 100 genes with the largest temporal
variance. Before fitting a VAR(1) model, we examine
their expression patterns to assess whether they
exhibit trends, oscillations, or abrupt changes.

```{r}
# Plot the first 10 selected genes
plot_genes <- top_genes[1:10]

plot_data <- data.frame(
  hour = 5:48,
  t(selected_expr[plot_genes, , drop = FALSE]),
  check.names = FALSE
)
# Convert to long format
plot_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
  plot_data,
  cols = -hour,
  names_to = "gene",
  values_to = "expression"
)

# Plot each gene across time
ggplot(plot_long, aes(x = hour, y = expression)) +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Expression of the 10 Most Variable Genes",
    x = "Developmental Time (Hours)",
    y = "log2(CPM + 1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Examining First Differences

The selected genes exhibit strong developmental
changes in their expression levels, suggesting
possible nonstationarity.

We examine first differences to determine whether
the hourly changes have more stable behavior.

```{r}
# First differences of log-normalized expression
diff_expr <- selected_expr[, -1, drop = FALSE] -
  selected_expr[, -ncol(selected_expr), drop = FALSE]

dim(diff_expr)

# Prepare data for plotting
# Plot only 10 genes, while differencing all 100
diff_data <- data.frame(
  hour = 6:48,
  t(diff_expr[plot_genes, , drop = FALSE]),
  check.names = FALSE
)

diff_long <- tidyr::pivot_longer(
  diff_data,
  cols = -hour,
  names_to = "gene",
  values_to = "change"
)

# Plot hourly changes
ggplot(diff_long, aes(x = hour, y = change)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, linetype = "dashed",
             color = "gray50") +
  geom_line(color = "steelblue", linewidth = 0.8) +
  facet_wrap(~ gene, scales = "free_y") +
  labs(
    title = "Hourly Changes in Gene Expression",
    x = "Developmental Time (Hours)",
    y = "Change in log2(CPM + 1)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```


## Measuring the Developmental Transition

The first-difference plots show substantial changes around
hours 28–38. We measure the proportion of squared hourly
changes occurring during this period.

```{r}
# Hours corresponding to first differences
diff_hours <- 6:48

# Define the developmental transition window
transition <- diff_hours >= 28 & diff_hours <= 38

# Sum of squared changes during the transition
transition_ss <- rowSums(
  diff_expr[, transition, drop = FALSE]^2
)

# Sum of squared changes across all hours
total_ss <- rowSums(diff_expr^2)

# Proportion of squared changes during transition
transition_fraction <- ifelse(
  total_ss > 0,
  transition_ss / total_ss,
  NA_real_
)

transition_results <- data.frame(
  gene = rownames(diff_expr),
  transition_fraction = round(transition_fraction, 3)
)

# Summary for all 100 genes
summary(transition_results$transition_fraction)

# First 10 genes
head(transition_results, 10)
```


## Preparing the VAR(1) Dataset

The first-differenced expression data contain 43 hourly
observations for 100 selected genes.

We transpose the matrix so that rows represent time points
and columns represent genes, as required by our VAR(1)
estimation functions.

Because several genes exhibit large developmental changes,
this dataset will be used for exploratory modeling rather
than assumed to be stationary.

```{r}
# Transpose: observations x genes
# Transpose to observations x genes
Y_diff <- t(diff_expr)

# Add time labels
rownames(Y_diff) <- paste0(6:48, "hr")

# Check dimensions
dim(Y_diff)

# Create processed directory
dir.create(
  "data/processed",
  recursive = TRUE,
  showWarnings = FALSE
)

# Save the 100-gene dataset
write.csv(
  Y_diff,
  "data/processed/GSE130811_VAR1_differenced_p100.csv"
)

# Inspect first observations
head(Y_diff[, 1:5])
```
